title_en: Zhou Fujun v. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Xushui County Branch — dispute over compensation for loss of deposit after reporting loss
keywords_en: civil; dispute over savings contract; first instance; basic people's court; Hebei Province; natural person; financial institution; General Principles of Civil Law; effectiveness of telephone loss reporting; bank's liability for fault; whether savings regulations apply to deposits of individual industrial and commercial households; ruling in favor of plaintiff; loss of passbook; telephone loss reporting; deposit withdrawn by impersonator; good faith
full_text_en:
Zhou Fujun v. Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank — Dispute over Compensation for Loss of Reported Lost Deposit Withdrawn by an Impersonator

Plaintiff: Zhou Fujun, male, 34 years old, an individual industrial and commercial household from Dazhuang Village, Xushui County, Hebei Province.

Defendant: Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank of Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yongtang, President of Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank.

Agents ad litem: Wang Xiaojuan and Gao Ping, lawyers from Baoding Prefecture Law Firm, Hebei Province.

Zhou Fujun filed a lawsuit with the Xushui County People's Court of Hebei Province against Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank for compensation for losses arising from the reported loss of a deposit that was subsequently withdrawn by an impersonator. The court, after a public trial, found the following facts:

In 1985, the plaintiff, Zhou Fujun, deposited RMB 10,894.71 in a current deposit account at the Financial Service Office affiliated with Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank. On the morning of March 3, 1989, Zhou Fujun withdrew RMB 3,000 from the Financial Service Office using his passbook, leaving a balance of RMB 7,894.71. On the afternoon of the same day, Zhou Fujun discovered that his passbook was lost. Since his home was far from the Financial Service Office, he immediately reported the loss by telephone to the Financial Service Office. Wang Tiequan, a staff member of the Financial Service Office, upon receiving the telephone report of loss, checked the account and found that the plaintiff's deposit had not been touched. During the telephone call, Zhou Fujun said to Wang Tiequan, "Keep an eye on it; don't let anyone withdraw it fraudulently." Wang Tiequan agreed and told Zhou Fujun to come to the Financial Service Office the next day. Thereafter, Wang Tiequan did not process the loss reporting procedures for Zhou Fujun in accordance with the bank's relevant regulations, nor did he inform other staff members of this matter. On the afternoon of the following day, when Zhou Fujun went to the Financial Service Office to complete the formal loss reporting procedures, he was informed that RMB 7,500 of his deposit had already been withdrawn by an impersonator. Zhou Fujun demanded that the defendant compensate him for the deposit withdrawn by the impersonator, but the defendant refused. Consequently, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting that the defendant compensate him for the economic losses thus incurred.

The defendant, Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank, admitted the facts alleged by the plaintiff but argued that the plaintiff, being an individual industrial and commercial household, did not fall within the scope of savings deposits, and therefore the provisions on reporting loss by telephone or correspondence concerning deposits as stipulated in the *Accounting and Cashiering System for Savings of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China* were not applicable. Accordingly, the defendant should not bear the liability for compensation.

The Xushui County People's Court held that: Article 75 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China* provides that the lawful income of citizens, including savings, shall be protected by state law, and no organization or individual may infringe upon it. Although the plaintiff, Zhou Fujun, was an individual industrial and commercial household, his current deposit with the defendant was a form of savings. Therefore, pursuant to Article 53 of the *Interim Measures for the Management of Savings Offices of the People's Bank of China* and Article 54 of the *Accounting and Cashiering System of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China*, where a depositor loses his passbook, "if the depositor, due to special circumstances at the time, can only report the loss orally or by telephone or correspondence, the bank must verify that the deposit indeed exists, then record in red ink in the summary column of the account page the words 'oral or telephone/correspondence report of loss on × year × month × day,' keep the page in a separate file, and at the same time notify the applicant to come and complete the formal loss reporting procedures on the same day or the following day; failure to do so within the time limit shall render the report void." Upon discovering the loss of his passbook, Zhou Fujun immediately reported the loss by telephone, and at that time the deposit had indeed not been withdrawn by any impersonator, which was in compliance with the above provisions. Zhou Fujun's home was more than 10 kilometers away from the Financial Service Office, and it was already around 4:00 p.m. when he reported the loss by telephone, making it impossible for him to travel to the defendant's place to complete the formal loss reporting procedures; this should be considered a special circumstance. The defendant's staff member, Wang Tiequan, after receiving Zhou Fujun's telephone report of loss, violated the bank's regulations by failing to record in red ink the words "oral report of loss" in the summary column of the account page and keep the page in a separate file, and on the following day, he failed to inform other staff members of the above situation and left his post without authorization, resulting in Zhou Fujun's reported lost deposit being withdrawn by an impersonator. Even if the defendant considered that Zhou Fujun's deposit was not subject to the provisions on oral or telephone/correspondence reporting of loss, since the bank staff member had agreed to the telephone report of loss, the bank should have performed its obligation to safeguard Zhou Fujun's deposit from being withdrawn by an impersonator in accordance with the agreement. Therefore, the defendant's defense was untenable. In accordance with Article 106, paragraph 1, of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, the defendant's staff, due to fault in failing to perform their obligations, caused property damage to others, and the defendant shall bear civil liability. In accordance with Article 134, item (7), of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, the defendant shall compensate for the losses. Regarding the calculation of interest on the plaintiff's deposit to be compensated by the defendant, due to the protracted litigation period and several changes in interest rates, both parties agreed to calculate interest at a monthly rate of 0.9%.

On the basis of finding the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, the defendant, Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank, requested mediation. The plaintiff, Zhou Fujun, agreed. On October 9, 1990, the Xushui County People's Court, pursuant to Article 97 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation)*, presided over mediation, and the following agreement was reached:

The defendant, Xushui County Industrial and Commercial Bank, shall pay the plaintiff, Zhou Fujun, RMB 7,500 as the principal of the deposit and RMB 1,279.73 as interest.
